arxiv-2102-07379.title: On the Inherent Regularization Effects of Noise Injection During Training
arxiv-2102-07379.creator: Oussama Dhifallah, Yue M. Lu
arxiv-2102-07379.description: Abstract Randomly perturbing networks during the training process is a commonly used approach to improving generalization performance. In this paper, we present a theoretical study of one particular way of random perturbation, which corresponds to injecting artificial noise to the training data.

arxiv-2104-04831.title: Search for \PWpr \PWpr bosons decaying to a top and a bottom quark at s = 13 ​ \TeV \sqrt{s}=13\TeV in the hadronic final state
arxiv-2104-04831.description: Abstract A search is performed for \PWpr \PWpr bosons decaying to a top and a bottom quark in the all-hadronic final state, in proton-proton collisions at a center-of-mass energy of 13 \TeV . The analyzed data were collected by the CMS experiment between 2016 and 2018 and correspond to an integrated luminosity of 137 \fbinv .

arxiv-2107-02027.title: Efficient Sequence Packing without Cross-contamination: Accelerating Large Language Models without Impacting Performance
arxiv-2107-02027.creator: Mario Michael KrellGraphcore Inc.United States of America mariok@graphcore.ai Matej KosecGraphcore Inc.United States of America matejk@graphcore.ai Sergio P. PerezGraphcore Inc.United Kingdom sergiop@graphcore.ai Andrew FitzgibbonGraphcore Inc.United Kingdom awf@graphcore.ai
arxiv-2107-02027.description: Abstract Effective training of today’s large language models (LLMs) depends on large batches and long sequences for throughput and accuracy. To handle variable-length sequences on hardware accelerators, it is common practice to introduce padding tokens, so that all sequences in a batch have the same length.

arxiv-2110-12439.title: Compositional data analysis — linear algebra, visualization and interpretation
arxiv-2110-12439.creator: Michael Greenacre
arxiv-2110-12439.description: Abstract Compositional data analysis is concerned with multivariate data that have a constant sum, usually 1 or 100%. These are data often found in biochemistry and geochemistry, but also in the social sciences, when relative values are of interest rather than the raw values. Recent applications are in the area of very high-dimensional “omics” data.

arxiv-2205-13565.title: Unequal Covariance Awareness for Fisher Discriminant Analysis and Its Variants in Classification
arxiv-2205-13565.creator: Thu Nguyen ⋆, Quang M. Le ⋆, Son N.T. Tu, Binh T. Nguyen
arxiv-2205-13565.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Thu Nguyen ⋆, Quang M. Le ⋆, Son N.T. Tu, Binh T. Nguyen. Fisher Discriminant Analysis (FDA) is one of the essential tools for feature extraction and classification. In addition, it motivates the development of many improved techniques based on the FDA to adapt to different problems or data types. However, none of these approaches make use of the fact that the assumption of equal covariance matrices in FDA is usually not satisfied in practical situations.

arxiv-2209-09838.title: On resolving conflicts between arguments
arxiv-2209-09838.description: Abstract Argument systems are based on the idea that one can construct arguments for propositions; i.e., structured reasons justifying the belief in a proposition. Using defeasible rules, arguments need not be valid in all circumstances, therefore, it might be possible to construct an argument for a proposition as well as its negation.

arxiv-2303-05150.title: Toward Higher Integration Density in Femtosecond-Laser-Written Programmable Photonic Circuits
arxiv-2303-05150.creator: Riccardo Albiero, Ciro Pentangelo, Marco Gardina, Simone Atzeni *, Francesco Ceccarelli and Roberto Osellame
arxiv-2303-05150.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Riccardo Albiero, Ciro Pentangelo, Marco Gardina, Simone Atzeni *, Francesco Ceccarelli and Roberto Osellame. Programmability in femtosecond-laser-written integrated circuits is commonly achieved with the implementation of thermal phase shifters. Recent work has shown how such phase shifters display significantly reduced power dissipation and thermal crosstalk with the implementation of thermal isolation structures. However, the aforementioned phase shifter technology is based on a single gold film, which poses severe limitations on integration density and circuit complexity due to intrinsic geometrical constraints.

arxiv-2404-18325.title: Canonical extensions via fitted sublocales
arxiv-2404-18325.creator: Tomáš Jakl, Anna Laura Suarez
arxiv-2404-18325.description: Abstract Abstract. We build on a result stating that the frame 𝖲𝖤 ⁡ ( L ) \mathsf{SE}(L) of strongly exact filters for a frame L L is anti-isomorphic to the coframe 𝒮 o ​ ( L ) \mathcal{S}_{o}(L) of fitted sublocales.

arxiv-2501-08676.title: FlexiClip: Locality-Preserving Free-Form Character Animation
arxiv-2501-08676.creator: Anant Khandelwal
arxiv-2501-08676.description: Abstract Animating clipart images with seamless motion while maintaining visual fidelity and temporal coherence presents significant challenges. Existing methods, such as AniClipart, effectively model spatial deformations but often fail to ensure smooth temporal transitions, resulting in artifacts like abrupt motions and geometric distortions.

arxiv-2601-03379.title: The interplay between topology, defects and chiral order in the nearly-commensurate charge density wave of 1T-TaS 2
arxiv-2601-03379.creator: Michael Verhage, Martin Lee, Kees Flipse
arxiv-2601-03379.description: Abstract In 1 T -TaS 2 , the nearly-commensurate charge density wave (NC-CDW) exhibits emergent chirality, a property of interest for technological applications such as memory. We study the relationship between chirality and topological defects using holographic analysis of scanning tunneling microscopy data.

arxiv-2606-30158.creator: B. Dudás, G. Papp, G. G. Barnaföldi, G. Bírófor the Bergen pCT Collaboration, [1ex] Institute for Physics, Eötvös Loránd UniversityPázmány Péter sétány. 1/A, 1117, Budapest, Hungary

europmc-pmc6441206.title: Ferroptosis, a new form of cell death: opportunities and challenges in cancer.
europmc-pmc6441206.creator: Mou Y, Wang J, Wu J, He D, Zhang C, Duan C, Li B.
europmc-pmc6441206.description: Ferroptosis is a novel type of cell death with distinct properties and recognizing functions involved in physical conditions or various diseases including cancers. The fast-growing studies of ferroptosis in cancer have boosted a perspective for its usage in cancer therapeutics....

pmc-10668980.title: Molecular Cloning, Heterologous Expression, Purification, and Evaluation of Protein–Ligand Interactions of CYP51 of Candida krusei Azole-Resistant Fungal Strain
pmc-10668980.creator: Tatsiana V Tsybruk, Leonid A Kaluzhskiy, Yuri V Mezentsev, Tatyana N Makarieva, Kseniya M Tabakmaher, Natalia V Ivanchina, Pavel S Dmitrenok, Alexander V Baranovsky, Andrei A Gilep, Alexis S Ivanov, Grishanova Alevtina
pmc-10668980.description: Due to the increasing prevalence of fungal diseases caused by fungi of the genus Candida and the development of pathogen resistance to available drugs, the need to find new effective antifungal agents has increased. Azole antifungals, which are inhibitors of sterol-14α-demethylase or CYP51, have been widely used in the treatment of fungal infections over the past two decades.

pmc-11360780.title: A Light-Powered Self-Circling Slider on an Elliptical Track with a Liquid Crystal Elastomer Fiber
pmc-11360780.creator: Lu Wei, Yanan Chen, Junjie Hu, Xueao Hu, Jiale Wang, Kai Li, Miguel Ángel López Manchado, Alexey Bubnov
pmc-11360780.description: In this paper, we propose an innovative light-powered LCE-slider system that enables continuous self-circling on an elliptical track and is comprised of a light-powered LCE string, slider, and rigid elliptical track. By formulating and solving dimensionless dynamic equations, we explain static and self-circling states, emphasizing self-circling dynamics and energy balance.

pmc-11495132.title: Five- and ten-year follow-up of medial unicompartmental knee arthroplasties in obese and non-obese patients
pmc-11495132.creator: Reinhold H Gregor, Gary J Hooper, Christopher Frampton
pmc-11495132.description: AimsThe aim of this study was to determine whether obesity had a detrimental effect on the long-term performance and survival of medial unicompartmental knee arthroplasties (UKAs).MethodsThis study reviewed prospectively collected functional outcome scores and revision rates of all medial UKA patients with recorded BMI performed in Christchurch, New Zealand, from January 2011 to September 2021.

pmc-11607836.title: Predicting solitary pulmonary lesions in breast cancer patients using 18fluorodeoxyglucose-positron emission tomography/computed tomography combined with clinicopathological characteristics
pmc-11607836.creator: Yangyang Xue, Weishu Hou, Yanhui He, Alei Xu, Xiaohu Li
pmc-11607836.description: BackgroundSolitary pulmonary nodules (SPNs) remain difficult to diagnose for clinical therapeutic purposes in patients with a history of breast cancer. This study try to investigate the value of 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose (18F-FDG) positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT) combined with clinicopathological predictors for the differential diagnosis of SPNs in breast cancer patients.

pmc-11614490.title: Allyl isothiocyanate exacerbates acute toxoplasmosis through inhibition of inflammatory cytokines
pmc-11614490.creator: Qiu-Mei Lin, Hong-Bin Long, Jun-Ting He, Zhi-hao Zhang, Ho-Woo Nam, Fu-Shi Quan, Qi Zhong, Xu-Qing Liu, Zhao-Shou Yang
pmc-11614490.description: Allyl isothiocyanate (AITC) is a natural product commonly used in food preservation and pharmaceutical applications. Toxoplasmosis, caused by the protozoan pathogen Toxoplasma gondii, is prevalent globally while the impact of AITC on toxoplasmosis is unclear. We explored the effect of AITC on acute toxoplasmosis. We infected C57BL/6 mice with T. gondii type I RH strain following AITC administration.

pmc-11636340.title: Shotgun metagenomics analysis indicates Bradyrhizobium spp. as the predominant genera for heavy metal resistance and bioremediation in a long-term heavy metal-contaminated ecosystem
pmc-11636340.creator: Rohan Agashe, Jonathan George, Ashish Pathak, Olasunkanmi Fasakin, John Seaman, Ashvini Chauhan
pmc-11636340.description: Ten soil cores were collected from the long-term heavy metal-contaminated Savannah River Site (SRS) and studied using shotgun metagenomics. In-line with our previous reports, Bradyrhizobium spp. dominated the SRS soils, and thus we recommend that SRS bioremediation studies target the Bradyrhizobium genus.

pmc-12462308.title: Movement and dietary behaviours and mental health among university students: the Health@NUS study
pmc-12462308.creator: Shenglin Zheng, Xin Hui Chua, Sarah Martine Edney, Claire Marie Goh, Bee Choo Tai, Janelle Chia, Daphne Koek, Rob M van Dam, Falk Müller-Riemenschneider
pmc-12462308.description: IntroductionUniversity years represent a crucial period in a student’s life, with mounting pressures on mental health and the formation of lifestyle habits that may endure into adulthood. This study examined the associations between movement and dietary behaviours and mental health among university students. It further explored potential sex-specific differences in these associations.

pmc-12677649.title: Soil Nutrient Enrichment Induces Trade‐Offs in Bacterial Life‐History Strategies Promoting Plant Productivity
pmc-12677649.creator: Yuanyuan Yan, Xing Zhou, Liangliang Liu, Zucong Cai, Josep Penuelas, Xinqi Huang
pmc-12677649.description: Despite the global prevalence of anthropogenic soil nutrient enrichment, its impacts on the trade‐offs in microbial life‐history strategies remain poorly understood, which is critical for agroecosystem productivity. Here, large‐scale observational studies are integrated with controlled experiments to systematically evaluate how soil nutrient enrichment affects bacterial functional potential and growth‐rate potential, ultimately determining microbial functions and plant productivity.

pmc-12706383.title: Primary Epstein-Barr Virus Infection Presenting as Cholestatic Hepatitis Without Infectious Mononucleosis in an Immunocompetent Middle-Aged Adult: A Case Report
pmc-12706383.creator: Mirac Burak Tak, Annabelle Li Kam Wa, Lauren Simkin, Mohamed Abdelnabi, Anika Tasneem
pmc-12706383.description: Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) infections commonly present with a subclinical hepatitis, often in the context of infectious mononucleosis (IM). A 56-year-old male presented with fever, alongside signs of jaundice and right upper quadrant tenderness. Initial investigations revealed marked cholestatic hepatic dysfunction, but imaging showed no evidence of biliary tree pathology.

pmc-12743542.title: Hydrogen excess drives metabolic reprogramming and viral dynamics in syngas-converting microbiomes
pmc-12743542.creator: Gabriele Ghiotto, Luca Francescato, Maria Agustina Biancalani, Laura Treu, Stefano Campanaro
pmc-12743542.description: Microbial communities drive essential bioprocesses, including the conversion of synthesis gas into biomethane, a sustainable energy source that supports circular carbon economies. In anaerobic environments, specialized consortia of bacteria and archaea facilitate syngas methanation through syntrophic interactions, where hydrogenotrophic methanogens play a central role in reducing carbon dioxide and monoxide with hydrogen.

pmc-12800865.title: Dermatological Manifestations of Amyloid Light-Chain (AL) Amyloidosis: A Case Report Highlighting Early Diagnosis and Treatment
pmc-12800865.creator: Shubhkaran Singh Gill, Teenu Kamboj
pmc-12800865.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). This case report describes a 52-year-old man who presented with gradually progressive dark cutaneous discoloration over the upper trunk and periorbital region, accompanied by painless enlargement of the tongue, which initially interfered with speech and eating. Over the subsequent months, he experienced marked unintentional weight loss, persistent fatigue, and symptoms consistent with autonomic involvement, including postural dizziness and altered bowel habits.

pmc-13049962.title: Lipid indices and coronary collateralization in STEMI: Expanding the metabolic perspective
pmc-13049962.creator: Ioannis Skalidis, Lisa Simioni, Mesmine Mawa Kamdem, Giulia S. Beretta, Serban Puricel
pmc-13049962.description: ute coronary occlusion [1]. In a cohort of 421 STEMI patients with acute total occlusion, higher levels of LDL-C, non-HDL-C, and the non-HDL-C/HDL-C ratio were independently associated with impaired CCC, with non-HDL-C demonstrating the strongest discriminatory ability for predicting poor collateralization. These findings support the concept that atherogenic lipid burden may influence ischemia-driven vascular remodeling.

pmc-13219525.title: Facies classification and channel detection for reservoir characterization using self-organizing maps in geologically complex Groningen gas field, the Netherlands
pmc-13219525.creator: Sarah El-Attar, Abdel-Khalek El-Werr, Eman Mohamed Abdel-Rahman, Mohamed Nabil Sobhy
pmc-13219525.description: Facies classification and channel detection remain challenging in geologically complex reservoirs. Faulting, thin-bed effects, and wavelet interference strongly influence seismic responses in such settings. This study presents an integrated multi-attribute seismic workflow utilizing Self-Organizing Maps (SOM) to enhance facies classification and delineate gas-bearing channels within the Permian Rotliegend reservoir of the Groningen Field, the Netherlands.

pmc-13248664.title: TusDCB-mediated tRNA sulfur modification is required for virulence and intestinal fitness in enterohemorrhagic Escherichia coli
pmc-13248664.creator: Yumika Sato, Kazutomo Suzue, Hideru Obinata, Mio Horinouchi, Ayako Takita, Mai Maruhashi, Yoji A. Minamishima, Haruyoshi Tomita, Hidetada Hirakawa
pmc-13248664.description: Sulfur modification of tRNAs enhances translational accuracy and efficiency, yet its contribution to bacterial pathogenesis remains poorly understood. In Escherichia coli, the TusDCB complex catalyzes 2-thiolation of wobble uridines in lysine-, glutamate-, and glutamine-decoding tRNAs. To investigate its role in intestinal virulence, we constructed an in-frame tusDCB deletion mutant in enterohemorrhagic Escherichia coli (EHEC).

pmc-13303428.title: Metals and Extremophilic Bacteria in Mining Environments: A Systematic Review
pmc-13303428.creator: Joseline Jiménez-Venegas, Leonardo Zamora-Leiva, Celián Román-Figueroa, Yasna Tapia, Manuel Paneque

pmc-13534415.title: A multidimensional risk prediction framework for malignant intestinal obstruction based on machine learning: computational model development and clinical validation
pmc-13534415.creator: Chuntao Song, Zian Cheng

pmc-13558509.title: Adherence to CAL/BDP PAD-Cream Influences Treatment Effectiveness and Preference in Scalp Psoriasis Under Real-Life Conditions: Results from the Prospective, Multicenter, Observational PRO-SCALP Study
pmc-13558509.creator: Anthony Bewley, Andreas Pinter, José Luis López Estebaranz, Jordi Galván, Víctor Sapena, Volker Koscielny
pmc-13558509.description: IntroductionScalp psoriasis is often associated with poor adherence to topical therapy. A novel formulation of calcipotriol and betamethasone dipropionate based on polyaphron dispersion (CAL/BDP PAD-cream) showed improved outcomes and satisfaction in the PRO-SCALP study, particularly in patients with high adherence.

pmc-13578468.title: Biosynthesis of vanillin glucoside in Escherichia coli
pmc-13578468.creator: Mingyu Tian, Jinyi Li, Yong Du, Xiaolin Shen, Jia Wang, Xinxiao Sun, Qipeng Yuan
pmc-13578468.description: Vanillin is a widely used flavor compound in the food, cosmetic, and pharmaceutical industries. Although microbial biosynthesis offers a green alternative to conventional chemical synthesis, challenges such as unstable heterologous enzyme expression, insufficient methyl donor supply, and product cytotoxicity limit de novo production. Here, we engineered Escherichia coli to produce vanillyl alcohol, vanillin, and vanillin glucoside directly from glycerol.

pmc-13672979.title: A snare-assisted pull-up technique for side-branch component delivery during thoracic endovascular aortic repair for distal aortic arch aneurysm using Gore Thoracic Branch Endoprosthesis
pmc-13672979.creator: Takehiro Suzuki, Takao Ohki, Kota Shukuzawa, Soichiro Fukushima, Makiko Omori, Hirotsugu Ozawa, Ryo Nishide, Daisuke Yamagishi
pmc-13672979.description: We report a case of thoracic endovascular aortic repair using a thoracic branch endoprosthesis for aneurysm enlargement caused by an endoleak after prior fenestrated repair. A 75-year-old man with previous left subclavian artery stenting presented with aneurysm growth. Advancement of the side-branch component through the pre-existing stent was difficult because of severe angulation, and standard push-up techniques failed.
